title: Ghost Attack: Trace the Ronin Bridge Heist
intro: Use the historical Ronin case (recorded real data, replayed through TRACEFUSE). Each answer is checked against prepared, sourced case labels — not against the live scoring engine.

checkpoints.title: The breach
checkpoints.prompt: Which transaction moved 173,600 ETH out of the bridge to the seed address? Paste the transaction hash.
hints: Open ChronoReplay and jump to 2022-03-23 ~13:29 UTC.
Look for an INTERNAL transfer into the seed — the bridge sends ETH via a contract call.
checkpoints.explanation: A withdrawERC20For call by the exploiter caused the Ronin Bridge contract to release 173,600 ETH as an internal transfer.

checkpoints.title: The victim contract
checkpoints.prompt: Which contract address released the funds?
hints: Select the edge carrying 173,600 ETH into the seed.
Its source node carries an explorer label.
checkpoints.explanation: 0x1A2a…54F2 is labelled 'Ronin Bridge V1' by the explorer; it is the sender of both exploit transfers.

checkpoints.title: The stablecoin leg
checkpoints.prompt: How many USDC were withdrawn in the second exploit transaction (whole tokens)?
hints: Filter the asset to USDC in Matrix Mode.

checkpoints.title: Official attribution
checkpoints.prompt: Which official list entry includes the seed address?
hints: Open the seed node's evidence panel and look for a sanctions listing.
checkpoints.explanation: OFAC added 'Digital Currency Address - ETH 0x098B…2f96' to the LAZARUS GROUP entry. A listing is a legal designation, not a technical proof of key control.

checkpoints.title: When was it designated?
checkpoints.prompt: On what date did OFAC add the address to the SDN list? (YYYY-MM-DD)
hints: The sanctions-history evidence links to the official notice.

checkpoints.title: Fragmentation
checkpoints.prompt: On 2022-03-28 the exploiter began splitting ETH into new wallets with equal tranches. What was the size of each first tranche (ETH)?
hints: The fusion graph marks near-equal splits as 'coordinated_split' (an algorithmic hypothesis).
checkpoints.explanation: Three 500 ETH transfers within six minutes to three fresh wallets — a structuring pattern, which on its own does not prove intent.

checkpoints.title: Into the fog
checkpoints.prompt: Traced wallets deposited ETH into a privacy protocol. Paste one of its contract addresses.
hints: Look at the 'Blind spots' / privacy gaps panel.
Its label comes from an OFAC designation notice.
checkpoints.explanation: Tornado Cash contracts (designated 2022-08-08, delisted 2025-03-21). Pooled deposits break the on-chain link — TRACEFUSE reports this as an unresolved gap instead of guessing withdrawals.

checkpoints.title: What a mention means
checkpoints.prompt: A GitHub issue contains the exploiter address. What does that establish by itself?
choices: Only that the public text contains the address string
The issue author controls the wallet
The wallet belongs to Lazarus Group
hints: Read the caveats on any address_mention evidence.
checkpoints.explanation: Public mentions are exact-string matches with context; they are weak evidence and never proof of ownership or culpability. In this case most mentions are developer tools using the address as a sanctioned-address test vector.
